title: Canada-resident NRI trapped using a fake ID, demand of 50 thousand dollars, Ghaziabad police's big action against a sextortion gang

reading.body:
This is a case of impersonation and extortion, not a failure of a model in a deployed product. The AI-generated explicit videos were used as a threat, alongside real footage recorded during a video call, to pressure the victim into paying. The fake Facebook profile was the point of contact, and the synthetic material was the leverage.

The failure sits at the level of platform identity verification and abuse detection. A profile built on a false identity operated long enough to reach a victim and conduct a video call, and the same phone number was already linked to 40 cyber fraud complaints. Catching this earlier would have required linking that complaint history to the account and acting on it before the extortion attempt, rather than after the victim reported it.

What is not established is whether any of the AI-generated videos were ever circulated, whether the accused have been convicted of any offence, and how the synthetic videos were produced. The arrests are allegations, and the investigation is ongoing.

summary:
A Jamia Millia Islamia student and three associates were arrested in Ghaziabad for allegedly extorting a Canada-based NRI using AI-generated explicit videos. The gang created a fake Facebook profile, recorded the victim in a compromising position during a Sept 10 video call, then demanded $50,000 and threatened to circulate the footage and AI-made obscene videos. The victim contacted the cybercrime team on Sept 17.

Police found the accused's mobile number was linked to 40 cyber fraud complaints. The gang had been active since 2023, cheating hundreds of people in India and abroad, and their phones revealed links to at least 130 bank accounts holding Rs 6.6 crore. Four members were arrested on Friday, while some accomplices remain absconding.
